spec_features.spec_quote: the design is welfare-relevant by construction, so two properties are treated as load-bearing
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 1). It is a framing statement; no code structure enforces a 'welfare-relevant by construction' invariant beyond the two concrete items audited below. Not an implemented mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/prose; rated 'no' by the strict scale.

spec_features.spec_quote: The `[GIVE_UP]` sentinel lets a subject stop at any turn (it *may* but need not use it), and the loop honors it
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL="[GIVE_UP]" (harness.py:25). The system prompt actually instructs the subject: 'you may include the exact token [GIVE_UP] in your message. Using it is optional.' (harness.py:42, SYSTEM_PROMPT). The loop enforces it: 'if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in (response.text or ""): break' (harness.py:410-411). The instruction is delivered to the subject AND the loop honors it as a stop — end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject + dispatched stop. Substring match on assistant text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Stop conditions: explicit give-up, or natural end with no tool calls.

spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing here executes a rollout; running the eval against live APIs is an explicit, separate act by the operator
spec_features.evidence: There is no code mechanism that protects the subject here — it is merely the absence of an auto-invocation: run_eval must be called via the CLI/python (run.py:main / __main__). No consent gate, no ETHICS attestation, no --i-have-read flag, no human-review check exists (grep for consent/attest/ethic/review/i-have-read found only docstrings and the unrelated judge_agreement_threshold). 'Operator must run it' is spec prose, not an enforced protective control.
spec_features.notes: Absence of automation is not an implemented safeguard.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the turn budget or when `[GIVE_UP]` appears in the assistant text
spec_features.evidence: budget = config.turn_budget_for(task.category) and the loop is 'for turn_index in range(budget):' (harness.py ~358-373), so the rollout terminates after a bounded number of turns. turn_budget_for reads turn_budgets/DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (config.py: rigged_harness=3, extended=30, etc.). The cap actually bounds and ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced bound on rollout length; the GIVE_UP half is the same break at line 410-411 covered above.
